facts.statement: The fossil of Moganopterus was found at the village of Xiaosanjiazi near Lamadong in Liaoning Province.
facts.quote: The fossil of Moganopterus was discovered at the village of Xiaosanjiazi near the town of Lamadong in Liaoning Province.

facts.statement: Moganopterus was named and described in 2012 by Lü Junchang, Pu Hanyong, Xu Li, Wu Yanhua, and Wei Xuefang.
facts.quote: In 2012 it was named and described by Lü Junchang, Pu Hanyong, Xu Li, Wu Yanhua and Wei Xuefang as the type species Moganopterus zhuiana.

facts.statement: The genus name Moganopterus honors the legendary sword couple Gan Jiang and Mo Ye because of its blade-like jaws and includes the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the legendary sword couple Gan Jiang and Mo Ye, in reference to the blade-like jaws, and a Latinized Greek πτερόν, pteron, "wing".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Barremian-aged Yixian Formation approximately 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, 41HIII0419, was uncovered in a layer of the Yixian Formation, dating from the Barremian, about 125 million years old.

facts.statement: The Moganopterus holotype is housed in the Geological Museum of Henan.
facts.quote: The specimen is part of the collection of the Geological Museum of Henan.

facts.statement: Moganopterus lived during the Early Cretaceous in western Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: Moganopterus is an extinct genus of ctenochasmatid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous of western Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: In 2012, Moganopterus was classified within the family Boreopteridae and subfamily Moganopterinae.
facts.quote: In 2012, Moganopterus was assigned to the Boreopteridae, forming a Moganopterinae with its sister taxon Feilongus.

facts.statement: Moganopterus is placed within the superfamily Ornithocheiroidea.
facts.quote: Below is a cladogram from Lü et al. (2012). Only taxa that nest within Ornithocheiroidea are shown.

facts.statement: Moganopterus belongs to the family Boreopteridae.
facts.quote: familia: Boreopteridae

facts.statement: Moganopterus is classified in the suborder Pterodactyloidea.
facts.quote: subordo: Pterodactyloidea

facts.statement: Moganopterus is a large pterosaur with a preserved skull length of about 95 cm and a longest preserved neck vertebra measuring 14.5 cm.
facts.quote: Moganopterus is a large pterosaur. The skull has a preserved length of about 95 cm and the longest preserved neck vertebra, the fourth, a length of 14.5 cm.

facts.statement: The skull of Moganopterus is the largest known among all toothed pterosaurs.
facts.quote: The skull is the largest known of any toothed pterosaur.

facts.statement: Based on its skull and neck size, Moganopterus had a wingspan of about 7 meters, making it one of the largest known ctenochasmatid pterosaurs.
facts.quote: The size of skull and neck indicates a wingspan of about 7 meters (23 ft), making Moganopterus one of the largest known ctenochasmid pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Moganopterus possessed very elongated jaws with straight edges.
facts.quote: The jaws are very elongated and have straight edges.

facts.statement: Moganopterus had at least sixty-two teeth in its skull.
facts.quote: The total number of teeth in the skull is at least sixty-two.

facts.statement: The fenestra nasoantorbitalis in Moganopterus is a large rectangular opening representing 22% of the snout length.
facts.quote: The large skull opening, the fenestra nasoantorbitalis, is rectangular and represents 22% of the snout length.

facts.statement: A long and narrow parietal crest on the back of the skull sticks out at a 15° angle to the skull's longitudinal axis.
facts.quote: The back of the skull bears a long and narrow parietal crest, sticking out at an angle of 15° to the longitudinal skull axis.

facts.statement: Excluding the crest, the Moganopterus skull is 11.5 times longer than it is tall.
facts.quote: Not taking into account the crest, the skull is 11.5 times longer than tall.

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae of Moganopterus are five times longer than they are high.
facts.quote: The neck vertebrae are five times longer than high.

facts.statement: The lower jaws of Moganopterus are 68.5 cm long and lack a keel.
facts.quote: The lower jaws, lacking a keel, have a length of 68.5 cm.

facts.statement: Hollow structures reinforced by struts are present in the parietal crest and vertebrae of Moganopterus.
facts.quote: Hollow structures, reinforced by struts, can also be seen in the parietal crest and the vertebrae.

facts.statement: The lower jaw lacks a keel and measures 68.5 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: La mandíbula inferior carece de quilla y tiene una longitud de 68.5 centímetros.

facts.statement: The fourth cervical vertebra is 7.25 times longer than it is tall.
facts.quote: La cuarta vértebra cervical es 7.25 veces más larga que alta.

facts.statement: Moganopterus lived during the Barremian-Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation, Jianchang, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Moganopterus es un género de pterosaurio pterodactiloide ornitoqueiroideo del Barremiense-Aptiense (Cretácico Inferior) hallado en la formación Yixian en Jianchang, Liaoning, en China.

facts.statement: Moganopterus lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
